input.reasoning:
Backlog totals 81 story points across 8 tasks. No historical velocity/actuals exist for this team, so I estimated hours per task using a standard consulting heuristic (~6-8 hours per story point, split across roles by task nature), then allocated across the 4 staffed roles in proportion to their FTE capacity and the nature of the work (backend-heavy for RBAC/payments/migration, frontend-heavy for design system/dashboard/invoice UI, QA across all functional stories, DevOps concentrated on CI/pipeline and migration cutover support).

Role capacity check (assuming a ~6-month, 26-week delivery window at 40 hrs/week/FTE):
- Backend Developer: 1.5 FTE => ~1,560 hours available
- Frontend Developer: 1.0 FTE => ~1,040 hours available
- QA Engineer: 0.6 FTE => ~624 hours available
- DevOps Engineer: 0.4 FTE => ~416 hours available

I allocated hours per task summing to totals below, then checked against these caps. DevOps and QA are the tightest constraints given low FTE, so I kept their allocations lean and flagged that DevOps in particular is thinly staffed relative to two infrastructure-heavy items (PW-1 CI/staging and PW-8 migration cutover).

Task-level hour allocation (Backend / Frontend / QA / DevOps):
- PW-1 CI pipeline & staging (5 pts): 20 / 0 / 10 / 60
- PW-2 Design system (8 pts): 10 / 190 / 20 / 0
- PW-3 Registration/login (8 pts): 110 / 60 / 40 / 8
- PW-4 RBAC (13 pts): 190 / 90 / 50 / 6
- PW-5 Customer dashboard (8 pts): 60 / 130 / 30 / 0
- PW-6 Invoice list/detail (5 pts): 50 / 90 / 24 / 0
- PW-7 Payment integration (13 pts): 220 / 40 / 60 / 16
- PW-8 Legacy data migration (21 pts): 260 / 0 / 40 / 90

Role hour totals:
- Backend Developer: 20+10+110+190+60+50+220+260 = 920 hours
- Frontend Developer: 0+190+60+90+130+90+40+0 = 600 hours
- QA Engineer: 10+20+40+50+30+24+60+40 = 274 hours
- DevOps Engineer: 60+0+8+6+0+0+16+90 = 180 hours

All within FTE capacity caps computed above, with some headroom for the two Backend/Frontend FTEs to absorb rework and PM coordination overhead, while QA and DevOps run closer to their ceiling (DevOps at ~43% utilization of a 6-month window on 0.4 FTE, which is appropriate given only two infra-heavy tasks).

- Backend Developer: 920 x 98.33 = 90,463.60
- Frontend Developer: 600 x 90 = 54,000.00
- QA Engineer: 274 x 70 = 19,180.00
- DevOps Engineer: 180 x 110 = 19,800.00
Labour subtotal = 183,443.60

Non-labour costs: Stripe integration test/sandbox fees, cloud staging environment costs, Oracle migration tooling/licensing, and a contingency buffer for the legacy migration task (historically high-risk, no actuals to calibrate against).

nonLabourLines.description: Stripe integration sandbox, PCI review, and transaction test fees
Oracle legacy DB access, extraction tooling, and migration licensing
Contingency buffer for legacy data migration risk (data quality/reconciliation)

assumptions: No historical actuals/spend data exist for this project yet; estimate is based on story-point-to-hour heuristics (~6-8 hrs/point) and typical role mix per task type, not empirical velocity.
Assumed a ~26-week (6-month) delivery window when checking hour allocations against FTE capacity.

DevOps Engineer (0.4 FTE, 180 hours allocated) is thinly staffed relative to the two infrastructure-heavy tasks (CI/staging setup and legacy migration cutover); this role is a scheduling risk and may bottleneck delivery timing even though cost is contained.

QA Engineer (0.6 FTE) hours were kept lean (274 hours total) and spread thinly across all 8 backlog items; deeper regression/security testing (especially for RBAC and payments) may require additional QA time not currently budgeted.

Legacy data migration (PW-8, 21 points) carries the highest cost and risk due to data quality unknowns in the source Oracle schema; a contingency line was added rather than inflating labour hours speculatively.
Backend Developer hours (920 of ~1,560 available) and Frontend Developer hours (600 of ~1,040 available) leave headroom for rework, code review, and PM/coordination overhead not separately itemized.
Non-labour costs are rough placeholders for cloud, Stripe fees, and Oracle tooling; actual vendor quotes should replace these once available.
Story points were treated as relative complexity indicators only; actual hours may vary significantly once technical spikes are done, particularly for PW-7 (Stripe) and PW-8 (migration).
